title: Ordinary nonreducedness spreads from the generic fibre
statement: Let $h:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $T$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point]. If the scheme-theoretic fibre $Z_\xi$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is not reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], then there is a nonempty open subset $W\subseteq T$ such that $Z_t$ is not reduced for every $t\in W$. No flatness, Noetherianity, or reducedness of $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generic-nilpotent-affine-preparation] to $h:Z\to T$. It gives $T'=T_{\mathrm{red}}$, $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, a nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T'$ with $A$ a domain, and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Z'\times_{T'}V$. Here $B$ is finite type over $A$, $b^n=0$ for $n\ge1$, and $b\otimes1\ne0$ over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. It also gives the homeomorphism $T'\to T$ and canonical identifications of all residue-field fibres.

Apply [lem-trf-annihilator-quotients-generic-free] to $A,B,b$: step 1 gives the domain, finite-type and generic nonvanishing hypotheses. Write $C=B/\operatorname{Ann}_B(b)$ and $D=B/bB$. Obtain $0
e g\in A$ and put $b_g=b/1$, $V_g=D(g)$, $Q=B_g/\operatorname{Ann}_{B_g}(b_g)$ and $R=B_g/b_gB_g$. The canonical identifications give $A_g$-linear isomorphisms $u:Q	o C_g$ and $v:R	o D_g$, with both targets free and $C_g
e0$. For a basis $(e_j)$ of $C_g$, $q=\sum_j a_ju^{-1}(e_j)$ iff $u(q)=\sum_j a_je_j$, uniquely with finite support; likewise for $v$ and $R$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. A nonzero $c\in C_g$ has $u^{-1}(c)
e0$, so $Q
e0$. Both $Q,R$ are free, and $b_g^n=(b^n)/1=0$.

By [lem-trf-generic-nilpotent-affine-preparation], $U_g=\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ is an affine open of $Y_g=Z'\times_{T'}V_g$ with its specified $A_g$-algebra structure. Fix $t'\in V_g$ and put $k=\kappa_{V_g}(t')$. Apply [lem-trf-free-annihilator-nonreduced-fibres] with $X=Y_g$, $U=U_g$, base $A_g$, element $b_g$ and field map $A_g\to\mathcal O_{V_g,t'}\to k$, using the freeness, nonzeroness and nilpotence verified in step 2: the fibre $Y_g\times_{V_g}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is nonreduced. The open inclusion identifies $\mathcal O_{V_g,t'}$ with $\mathcal O_{T',t'}$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and hence identifies their quotients by maximal ideals, $k\cong\kappa_{T'}(t')$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Under this identification, $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V_g\to T'$ is the canonical point morphism because it induces that local-ring quotient [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Iterated base change [def-pc-base-change] therefore gives $Y_g\times_{V_g}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong Z'\times_{T'}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong Z'_{t'}$, preserving the projections to $Z'$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Isomorphic local rings have the same nilpotents, so reducedness of $Z'_{t'}$ would contradict the nonreduced fibre just obtained [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

Let $i:T'\to T$ be the homeomorphism of [lem-trf-generic-nilpotent-affine-preparation] and put $W=i(V_g)$. The set $V_g$ is open in $V$, hence in $T'$, so $W$ is open. Since $A$ is a domain and $g\ne0$, its prime $(0)$ belongs to $V_g=D(g)$; thus $W\ne\varnothing$. For $t\in W$, its unique preimage $t'$ belongs to $V_g$. Step 3 gives $Z'_{t'}$ nonreduced and preparation gives $Z'_{t'}\cong Z_t$. Were $Z_t$ reduced, the isomorphic local rings of $Z'_{t'}$ would have no nonzero nilpotents: a nilpotent maps to zero and injectivity makes it zero. This contradicts [def-pc-reduced-scheme].
